quote: Customer (Corbel) may not assign the Supply Agreement without Supplier's prior written consent. Supplier (Vantrell) may assign to "any Person without the consent of Customer, including in connection with a merger, consolidation, or sale of all or any part of Supplier's resin business." ... Post-Closing, Vantrell can sell its business (or the specific product lines) to a competitor, a less reliable supplier, or a strategic acquirer with no obligation to obtain Corbel's consent... Corbel would have no say in who its sole-source supplier is.
reason: Issue 7 of the memo cites Supply Agreement § 16.1. It sets out the one-sided assignment right: Supplier may assign without the Customer's consent, but the Customer needs the Supplier's consent. It then explains the risk that the sole-source supply contract could pass to a competitor or another undesirable party. It also recommends raising a mutual-consent requirement or a competitor carve-out in the Vantrell consent negotiation. This matches the ledger's expected finding.
